seam: OfferCard.handleAccept — on outcome.type === 'success', fire-and-forget reconcileActiveRide('').then(r => { if (r.outcome === 'active' && r.order) setOrder(r.order) }) BEFORE applyDecision/onDismiss. setOrder is obtained via an ATOMIC useActiveOrderStore(s => s.setOrder) selector.
seam_rationale: The accept-success path is the direct, race-free trigger — the POST /orders/{id}/accept has committed server-side before reconcile runs, so GET /drivers/me now carries the activeOrderId (AC#6 authoritative). Reuses the existing reconcileActiveRide (does NOT write a parallel hydration path). OfferCard is session-wide in DriverLayout, so it hydrates the store regardless of which /driver sub-route the driver is on, and the state-driven DriverMapScreen renders RideSheet with NO route change. reconcileActiveRide ignores its myDriverId arg (does `void myDriverId`) and fetches GET /drivers/me itself, so no useDriverMe/QueryClient dependency was introduced into OfferCard (which renders under only I18n+Theme in its tests). Fire-and-forget (not awaited) keeps the pre-existing no-navigate + onDismiss contract intact; the new test awaits the store write via findBy*. useRideRestore's mount-only behavior is UNCHANGED (extended, not broken).
new_test_note: acceptHydration.test.tsx composes <OfferCard> + <DriverMapScreen> as siblings sharing the module-global zustand store, STARTING FROM AN EMPTY STORE, with REAL useActiveOrder + REAL useActiveOrderStore (unlike WI-5's DriverMapScreen.test.tsx which vi.mock'd useActiveOrder to already return an order — the gap that let the defect ship). Only useOfferAccept (accept POST) and reconcileActiveRide are mocked; a successful accept must flow through the real store into the real DriverMapScreen and paint RideSheet's 'Jsem na místě'. This pins the accept->hydration contract so a regression goes RED without the e2e.
